result.rationale: In Ruby, `^` anchors to the start of any line, so `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (line 12 of TopicEmbed.import) accepts values like "javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x". The diff then interpolates the URL unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` in the imported_from footer, and cook_method raw_html means the content is stored/rendered as-is. The URL flows in from external RSS items (i.link / i.id in poll_feed.rb) and embed_url params, so the mechanism described is verifiable in the diff and constitutes a real validation bypass.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the guard `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses `^` rather than `\A`, so it can match at the start of any line within a multi-line string (e.g., a value containing a newline before an `http://...` line). Immediately after, `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML string (`"#{url}"`) that is later posted with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, meaning no cooking/sanitization occurs. This makes the URL validation weaker than intended and can allow unsafe/harmful URLs to be embedded into rendered HTML (at minimum a security/correctness issue).
